hints: Focus on what NaBH4 actually does, it reduces the C=O of aldehydes and ketones to an alcohol but leaves a C=C alone.
Draw the alcohol product for compound 1, pentan-2-one gives CH3CH2CH2CH(OH)CH3, now check the four groups on that C-OH carbon.
Apply the same test to the other two products and remember a carbon with two identical ethyl groups cannot be chiral, so pick the combination that works.
walkthrough:
**Recall NaBH4 reduction**

NaBH4 is a selective reducing agent. It adds H to the carbonyl carbon to turn a ketone into a secondary alcohol.

$$\text{R-CO-R' + [H] } \xrightarrow{\text{NaBH}_4} \text{ R-CH(OH)-R'}$$

**Draw product 1 and test for chirality**

Compound 1 is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COCH}_3$ (pentan-2-one). Reduction gives pentan-2-ol.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$$
The C-2 bears four different groups: $\text{H}$, $\text{OH}$, $\text{CH}_3$ and $\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. So it is chiral. Statement 1 is correct.

**Draw product 2 and test for chirality**

Compound 2 is $\text{CH}_2\text{=CHCOCH}_2\text{CH}_3$ (pent-1-en-3-one). NaBH4 reduces only C=O, not C=C, giving pent-1-en-3-ol.

$$\text{CH}_2\text{=CH-CH(OH)-CH}_2\text{CH}_3$$
The C-3 bears $\text{H}$, $\text{OH}$, $\text{CH=CH}_2$ and $\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. All four are different, so it is chiral. Statement 2 is correct.

**Draw product 3 and test for chirality**

Compound 3 is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3$ (pentan-3-one). Reduction gives pentan-3-ol.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$$
The C-3 bears $\text{H}$, $\text{OH}$ and two identical $\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ groups. With only three distinct groups it is achiral. Statement 3 is incorrect.

**Conclude the combination**

Only 1 and 2 give a chiral alcohol product. That matches option B.

options.A: Incorrect if this is 1, 2 and 3. Compound 3 gives CH3CH2CH(OH)CH2CH3 where the central carbon has two identical ethyl groups, so it is not chiral. This trap comes from forgetting to check for identical alkyl groups.
options.B: Correct for 1 and 2 only. Both reductions create a C bearing H, OH and two different carbon chains, so both products contain a chiral centre, while 3 does not.
options.C: Incorrect if this is 2 and 3 only. It correctly includes 2 but wrongly includes the symmetrical product 3 and wrongly excludes 1, which clearly forms chiral pentan-2-ol.
options.D: Incorrect if this is 1 only. It misses compound 2. Students choose this by thinking NaBH4 also reduces the C=C bond, but NaBH4 leaves the alkene intact, so the unsaturated alcohol from 2 is still chiral.
